intro: Carmarthen, in Carmarthenshire, Wales, has one tree on our map: a ginkgo in the garden of the library at the Carmarthen campus of the University of Wales Trinity Saint David on College Road. A reader photographed it in its autumn gold, in the rain, and says the library's large windows look straight onto it. They put its age at about 180 years, reasoning that the campus opened in 1842. It is a guess rather than a record, and the gold is brief.

trees.name: The Library Ginkgo of Carmarthen

trees.story:
A ginkgo in the garden of the library at the Carmarthen campus of the University of Wales Trinity Saint David turns a deep gold each autumn, and a reader sent us a photograph of it in the rain. The library has large glass windows that look onto the garden, and the reader says that in autumn the tree “shines its glory through those windows.”

In the photograph two crowns rise together out of one mass of leaves, every one the same bright yellow, against a grey sky. A white balcony and a slope of roof sit at the left edge of the frame, the grass below is green, and a few leaves are already on the ground.

The reader adds a guess at the age. The campus opened in 1842, and if the tree is as old as the campus it is about 180 years. That is their reasoning, not a record, and we have found no planting date or measurement for it.

Ginkgo leaves drop within a few days of turning, so the gold is brief.

question_meta: A ginkgo turns gold in the library garden of the Carmarthen campus. Where it is and what a reader says about it.
question_answer: A reader photographed a ginkgo (Ginkgo biloba) in the garden of the library at the Carmarthen campus of the University of Wales Trinity Saint David. They estimate it at about 180 years, as old as the campus, which opened in 1842.
question_context: Everything this page says comes from one reader's photograph and note, sent through the app with a GPS fix taken where they stood. The age of about 180 years is the reader's reasoning from the campus opening in 1842, not a record, and we have found no planting date, girth or height for the tree. The photograph shows a ginkgo whose crown is made of two tall stems rising together, every leaf the same bright yellow, against a grey sky, with a white balcony and a slope of roof at the left edge of the frame. The tree stands in the garden beside the library, on a university campus, and we found no published opening terms for the grounds, so follow any signs. If you know when the tree was planted, or have measured it, tell us on the page and it goes into this answer. We would also like to know its height, if anyone can say.
